title: An Inactive tab emptied by a search shows the usual no-match result
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have an inactive part, part A, in category A, so the category B filter leaves it out.
  • Use a second category, category B, that part A is not in.
  • Use a search text that matches no part at the test location, active or inactive.
  • Start on the Inventory page (Parts in the top bar, then Inventory in the left menu), on the Active tab.
custom_steps:
1. Type the search text that matches no part in the Search box.
  2. Click the Inactive tab.
  3. Type the search text that matches no part in the Search box again.
  4. Replace the search text with part A's part number.
  5. Pick category B in the Category filter.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The Active tab shows the list's usual empty result for a search that matches nothing (write its wording in the result comment).

Step 2:

  • The Inactive tab is selected.

Step 3:

  • The Inactive tab shows the same empty result as the Active tab did in step 1.
  • It does not say "No inactive parts at this location."

Step 4:

  • Part A is listed.

Step 5:

  • With the search and the category B filter leaving nothing, the Inactive tab again shows the usual empty result.
  • It does not say "No inactive parts at this location."

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10814 (Story 1, Active and Inactive Tabs on the Inventory List)

  • S1-N2: “If a search or filter leaves the Inactive tab empty, it shows the list's standard filtered empty state.”
  • S1-N1: “If there are no inactive parts at the location and no search or filter is narrowing the list, the Inactive tab shows "No inactive parts at this location."”
